definitions.coins: The 100 largest coins by market cap on CoinGecko, on every chain, in CoinGecko's order; rank is CoinGecko's market-cap rank.
definitions.bubble: Bigger bubble = bigger market cap, on a compressed scale (a bubble's area grows with the square root of its market cap), but no bubble is smaller than its ticker needs to be read at the text floor (a long ticker wraps at its own '_', '.', '-' or '/'). A bubble held at that size is sized by its ticker, not its market cap: on a narrow screen most bubbles are, and a coin with a long ticker can be drawn bigger than coins with larger market caps — the map's caption says how many at the reader's width. The three largest coins are always the three biggest bubbles, in order. The exact share of the market is the Dominance figure in each coin's tooltip, card and the list. A coin with no market cap is listed and not drawn.
definitions.colour: Colour: the 24 h price change, in the legend's nine steps — brighter for a bigger move, up or down; a coin CoinGecko gives no change for is outlined and hatched ("no 24 h change given"), never drawn as 0%.
definitions.change24h: CoinGecko's change in the coin's US-dollar price over the last 24 hours, in percent (−5.27 means down 5.27%); null with why when CoinGecko gives none, never 0.
definitions.dominance: The coin's market cap as a share of CoinGecko's total market cap of every coin it lists, in percent (59.6 means 59.6%; its /global read, every 30 minutes, which the label names). Worked out by this site from CoinGecko's two figures, and as old as the older of them (its at); none when the market cap is not CoinGecko's own, or the total and the coins were read more than 2 hours apart.
definitions.volume24h: CoinGecko's trading volume over the last 24 hours, every market it tracks.
definitions.stable: true when CoinGecko files the coin in its stablecoins category (read every 6 hours); null until that list has been read.
definitions.check: The market cap checked against CoinLore's 100 largest coins, by the chain market caps' rules (lib/chainmcap.js): its coin counts when its symbol, name and price (within 10%) are CoinGecko's on the same read, or — under another name (CoinLore calls BNB "Binance Coin") — when its symbol and a price within 3% are and no other coin with that symbol among those 100 is priced within 10%, which the check says, with CoinLore's name; for a coin under $0.0001, whose price CoinLore rounds to 6 decimal places, CoinLore's own market cap ÷ circulating supply is the price compared; "agreed" within 10%, "differs" (the notes say why from the numbers), "single" (one source; the notes say why).
definitions.total: CoinGecko's total market cap of every coin it lists — not only the 100 drawn.
definitions.logo: The coin's picture as CoinGecko gives it, served through this site's own image proxy (/api/market/logo) — never fetched by your browser from CoinGecko; null when CoinGecko gives none, or when it would be Robinhood's artwork (a Robinhood Chain token's picture named after its own address, or a Robinhood Stock Token's).
definitions.onchain: Where the coin's on-chain data is on this site, from CoinGecko's list of every coin's contract addresses (read once a day): "contract" — its contract on Robinhood Chain, Ethereum or Solana (preferred in that order), which the Scanner profiles (scannable: true); "quote" — its contract there is a base trading asset, a stablecoin or wrapped coin other tokens are priced in (WETH, USDG, USDC, USDT, DAI, WBTC, wrapped SOL), which the Scanner does not profile; "native" — no such contract, and the coin is the own coin of a chain Market Data reads (DefiLlama names it), whose chain view has its figures; "none" — no contract on those three chains that CoinGecko lists, and not the own coin of a chain Market Data reads. onchain is null, with onchainWhy saying why, until CoinGecko's list (or, for a coin with no contract there, DefiLlama's list of chains) has been read; onchainWhy is null otherwise.

notes: Not advice, never a tip to buy. Do your own research.
The 100 largest coins by market cap on CoinGecko, on every chain, read every 10 minutes; CoinGecko's total market cap every 30 minutes; its stablecoins category every 6 hours.

Each market cap is looked up in CoinLore's 100 largest coins: 68 of these 100 were found there and compared (34 agree, 34 differ by more than 10%); 32 have one source — the chip on each coin says which.
